A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Traversal Verification work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original acceptance-length and throughput experiments on Llama model pairs, including tree-size, chain-depth, and temperature analyses in Tables 2–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original generation-quality scores and Vicuna-based aggregation comparisons in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 and its probability-update equations are unchanged. Appendices E–F explain the existing post-order traversal and sequence-level RRSw interpretation; they introduce no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six Spec-Bench tasks. The added quality evaluation uses MT-Bench, already represented in v1; the additional Vicuna model pair changes model configuration rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Token-level RRSw remains the verification comparator, and autoregressive generation already appears as a throughput reference in v1. The added quality comparison reuses these methods; Gemini-2.5-Flash is an evaluator, not a decoding baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds a 10-point generation-quality evaluation using Gemini-2.5-Flash. Appendix D adds an EAGLE-Vicuna-7B-v1.3/Vicuna-7B-v1.3 configuration evaluated under pooled and per-item acceptance-length aggregation. The original experiments retain their stated settings.

E4.justification: New Appendices C–D examine preservation of generation quality and sensitivity to acceptance-length aggregation. The existing chain-depth/tree-size analysis in Figure 3 and temperature analysis in Table 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly documents per-item averaging and compares it with pooled aggregation, adding statistical-estimation detail. Three-run averaging and the original standard-error reporting remain unchanged; no additional seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 and Figure 3 retain their results. New Table 5 reports quality scores of 6.72 for autoregressive generation and 6.77, 6.79, and 6.74 for Traversal on chain, sparse-tree, and binary-tree configurations. Table 6 adds Vicuna results, including chain speedups of 1.77x for token-level verification and 1.81x for Traversal.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 replaces the path-product condition with an autoregressive decoding-tree definition explicitly allowing sampling with or without replacement. Appendices A–B revise probability conditioning, correct a summation index, and add an explicit expectation over sampled chains to the optimality derivation. The principal theorem statements are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its performance comparison from 'existing methods' to 'token-level verification'. The principal contributions concerning losslessness, single-chain optimality, token utilization, and acceleration remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix G explicitly states that greedy decoding offers no benefit and proposes low-probability pruning as possible overhead mitigation. Appendices C–D explain why empirical quality checks cannot prove losslessness and why pooled aggregation emphasizes long responses. Verification overhead was already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix I adds URLs and licenses for model, benchmark, and code assets. Appendices C–E document the judge and additional model configuration, per-item averaging, and post-order DFS. These additions improve reproducibility information without establishing that the retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Gemini 2.5 reference and explicitly adopts Medusa's generation-quality evaluation approach. The related-work discussion otherwise retains its positioning; Block Verification's updated publication metadata represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized revisions to the abstract, theoretical exposition, and experimental setup, retitles Appendix B, and adds Appendices C–I. Contact information, conference identification, and acknowledgments are added while the main section structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–7 and the sequence-level RRSw illustration in Figure 4. Figure 3 moves from page 8 to page 9, with surrounding material reflowed. Existing figures and performance-table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's reliance on theory for generation quality and unspecified acceptance-length aggregation, v2 adds supporting quality measurements, explains and tests aggregation choices, and explicitly states the greedy-decoding limitation. Asset links and licenses also improve transparency. These are useful, limited gains: the original algorithm and results remain stable, and the single-judge quality averages do not establish exact distributional equivalence.
